creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`enum`, `regex` and `range` are accepted on a list or variadic arg, shown nowhere, and never enforced:

```rad
args:
    scores int[]
    scores range [0, 100]
```

```
$ rad script.rad --scores 5 --scores 500
scores=[ 5, 500 ]
```

Same for `enum` on `str[]` (`--envs nope` passes) and `regex` on `*tags` (`ABC` and `123` pass). `rad check` reports no diagnostics, and the constraint never reaches `-h` - the args block shows a bare `--scores ints` where the scalar equivalent shows `Range: [0, 100]`.

The scalar path works, so an author has every reason to believe the list one does. A script validating `*envs str enum [...]` before feeding those values into a shell command is trusting something that isn't happening.

Visible on both sides of the boundary: the four `*ListRadArg` types in `core/args.go` carry no `EnumConstraint`, `RegexConstraint` or `RangeConstraint` field, and `ra`'s slice flags expose no constraint setters at all. So this is Rad wiring plus per-element validation in `ra`.

The natural reading is per-element:

```rad
args:
    scores int[] range [0, 100]
    *envs str enum ["dev", "stg", "prd"]
    *tags str regex "[a-z][a-z0-9-]*"
```

Minimum bar is rejecting a declaration that can't be honored rather than ignoring it. Enforcing per-element is the better answer.

Enforcing will fail scripts that currently pass values violating a declared-but-ignored constraint - which is the point, but it needs a migration note.

`run-the-nine` lists regex-on-variadics as an unverified probe; this resolves it.
title: Scalar arg constraints are silently ignored on list and variadic args
